steps_guide.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Becoming a Category B Driver (Car / Light Van)

step_1.title: 1. Prepare for the Theory Test
step_1.text_1: Handbook: Begin by carefully studying the
step_1.text_2: This is the official source of knowledge about Ireland's road rules.
step_1.text_3: Pay special attention to sections on road signs, road markings, speed limits, priority rules, and road behavior in various situations.
step_1.text_5: Learning road signs is an important part of your preparation, helping you become more comfortable on the road and pass the theory test successfully.
step_1.text_7: regularly. This will help you get used to the structure of the exam and the types of questions you may encounter.
step_1.text_8: After each test, review your mistakes and revise the topics you find difficult.

step_2.title: 2. Take the Theory Test
step_2.text_1: Book your test: Register on the official website
step_2.text_2: choose a nearby test center and a convenient time. Detailed
step_2.text_3: can be found on our website.
step_2.text_4: Exam: The theory test consists of 40 questions, and you need at least 35 correct answers to pass. The allotted time is 45 minutes.
step_2.text_5: Once you pass the test, you will receive a Certificate of Competency.

step_3.title: 3. Apply for a Learner Permit
step_3.text_1: Now you can apply online for a Learner Permit, simplifying the process. There’s no need to fill in paper forms, book appointments, or visit NDLS in person. To apply online, simply click
step_3.text_2: To submit your application, you will need:
step_3.li_1: A Public Services Card and a verified
step_3.li_2: Proof of having successfully passed the theory test in the appropriate category within the last 2 years.
step_3.li_3: A fully completed Eye Report Form, dated within the last 1 month, if required in your case.
step_3.li_4: A fully completed Medical Report Form, dated within the last 1 month, if required in your case.
step_3.li_5: Proof of address, issued within the last 6 months, if your current address is different from the one you previously provided when applying for your PSC.
step_3.li_6: Proof that you normally reside in Ireland, if your place of birth and citizenship are outside the EU/EEA.
step_3.li_7: A completed Certificate of Professional Competence (CPC) if required.
step_3.text_3: The application fee is €45.00. You can pay by credit or debit card. If you are 70 or over, you are exempt from this fee.

step_4.title: 4. Practical Training
step_4.text_1: Find an Instructor or Driving School: Find a qualified instructor registered with the RSA (Road Safety Authority). Make sure the instructor holds an Approved Driving Instructor (ADI) certificate.
step_4.text_2: Essential Driver Training (EDT) Lessons: In Ireland, you must complete 12 hours of mandatory lessons. The course covers all key aspects of driving.
step_4.text_3: Practice with a Supervisor: You may practice with an experienced driver who has held a full license for at least 2 years. The car must display an “L” (Learner) plate at the back and the front.

step_5.title: 5. Prepare for the Driving Test
step_5.text_1: Complete EDT: After finishing all 12 lessons, your instructor will fill in your EDT Logbook, which you must present at your driving test.
step_5.text_2: Practice in real conditions: Drive regularly under real road conditions to improve your skills.

step_6.title: 6. Take the Driving Test
step_6.text_1: Book your test: Register for your test on
step_6.text_1_extend: Choose a nearby center and convenient time.
step_6.li_1: You should arrive 10–15 minutes before your appointment.
step_6.li_2: Don’t forget to bring your Learner Permit and any other documents you may need (such as booking confirmation).
step_6.li_3: The tester will check your documents and identification. They may also ask you to show that your vehicle meets requirements (such as having a valid insurance policy).
step_6.li_4: Before the test starts, the tester may ask you to perform some vehicle checks, like testing brakes, indicators, and lights.
step_6.li_5: The test starts once you take the driver's seat and the tester sits in the passenger seat.
step_6.li_6: You will be required to perform a range of tasks on the road, including starting, braking, changing lanes, turning, reversing, and parking.
step_6.li_7: The tester assesses how you handle different road situations, obey road rules, use mirrors and signals, and control the vehicle safely.
step_6.li_8: Your ability to maneuver safely in heavy or challenging conditions will also be evaluated.
step_6.li_9: Once you complete all the tasks, you will return to the test center.
step_6.li_10: After finishing the test, the tester will tell you whether you have passed. If you pass, you will be issued a temporary Certificate of Competency while you wait for your driving license.
step_6.li_11: If you fail, the tester will explain where you made mistakes and give recommendations for improvement.

step_7.title: 7. Obtain a Full Driving License
step_7.text_1: After successfully passing the driving test, you can apply for a full driving license. This can be done online through
step_7.text_1_extend: or in person at any National Driver Licence Service (NDLS) center.
step_7.li_2: Proof of address if it’s different from previously provided.
step_7.li_3: A recent color photo (if applying in person).
step_7.li_5: A completed application form (if applying in person).
step_7.li_6: Pay the appropriate license fee. The amount depends on the license's validity (typically 10 years).
step_7.li_7: Once processed, your full driving license will be issued and may be posted to your address.
step_7.li_8: If you previously held a temporary license, you must surrender it when you get your full license.
step_7.li_9: A full driving license in Ireland is typically valid for 10 years. After this, it must be renewed.
